phase: 2 independent lexical and grammar freeze before exact candidate
method: Actual full photos personally viewed, not extracted prose, locator names, citation index, or English translations of the verse. Full relevant Latin entries/continuations and actual printed grammar patterns assessed. No candidate yet opened.
source_reaffirmation: Initial own transcription retained pending byte comparison. Verse includes initial conjunction, finite mixing verb, total quantity, two plural water occurrences, bracketed relative before with, upper relative, heavens, male predicate and masculine copula, conjunction plus singular water, lower relative, earth, female predicate and feminine copula.

lexical_controls.finding: Ground/intensive entry has miscere, immittere, adjungere; reflexive/passive III,1 and 2 has misceri/commisceri/admisceri/immisceri, then conjungi/copulari/consociari and further communion/matrimonial senses. Liquid sense suits waters. Hen54:8 citation is not used as a finite paradigm. No expressed external mixing agent is licensed.
Universitas, omne, omnis; adjectival quantity and all/every usages. Here quantity attaches first plural waters, not heavens or a supplied class of beings.

Actual water entry at 212 identifies aqua and plural ማያት, plural frequent in Bible with both masculine/feminine verb possibilities and singular also in use. Source plurality must not be silently rewritten throughout.

Preposition with/alongside and relational constructions. Whole preceding/continued comparative and communion uses read; mixing plus waters calls for with rather than a free equivalence or like reading.
Actual upper preposition entry: in superiore parte, super; upper/above spatial relation. Not an adjective describing sex, not a new heavenly agent.
Coelum, both grammatical genders, plural heavens form. Here governed by upper relation.
mas, masculus, de hominibus and examples; male predicate as opposed to female is justified. Fortis/virilis root meanings do not displace explicit male/female contrast.

Third-person pronoun male and female forms, with actual nominal-sentence and pro copula uses in continuation at 919. Here is serves nominal predication; English can keep singular is for the upper plural construction by explanatory note rather than normalize source to two singular waters.
Copulative et, joins verbs/sentences; initial And and lower-water and licensed. Not temporal then as an independently printed word.
Pars vel locus inferior and preposition infra/subter, inferior location. Source lower relative refers beneath earth.
Terra, orbis terrarum and further land/soil senses; here spatial earth suitable.

lexical_controls.entry: እንስት / እንስታይት and surrounding continued context
lexical_controls.finding: Female sex/femina; adjective femininus at 772, including spelling variants and other references. Morphological female predicate is not inferred solely from the verse citation.

Relative qui/quae/quod; nominal/preposition attachment and number variation documented. Printed bracketed initial relative is distinct from two unbracketed relatives introducing above/below; it must be retained in diplomatic source and accounted editorially, not silently normalized.

finite_form_and_mood.own_analysis: ወ + ይደመሩ: conjunction plus prefixed third-person masculine plural -u reflexive/passive form of d-m-r; underlying formative t before d assimilates (103 §54; 191 §97). III,1 reflexive can be read yə[t]dämar-u (unwritten assimilation/gemination); III,2 subjunctive spelling is also relevant, not to be selected merely by lexical Hen citation. Printed first radical first-order ደ is material.
finite_form_and_mood.patterns_actually_read: 103 assimilation to d/t; 167-170,172 temporal imperfect versus indicative terminology and future use; 173-175 subjunctive force and tense formation; 191-195 III reflexive paradigms, III,1 identity of imperfect/subjunctive, III,2 first-radical contrast; 202-204 third-person prefix plus masculine plural -u.
finite_form_and_mood.mood_limit: The written III,1 form does not by itself distinguish indicative imperfect from subjunctive/jussive. No claim of a uniquely encoded indicative ending is warranted. A predictive future is contextually defensible as continuation of the apocalyptic prospective sequence; jussive requires a command/wish justification beyond this isolated form.
finite_form_and_mood.temporal_force: Prospective will/be mixed is a contextual translation judgment, not a morphologically unique future tense. Do not label an active they mix or name an unprinted agent.
finite_form_and_mood.confidence: medium for prefix/plural/passive-reflexive and contextual future; low for uniquely disambiguating mood from orthography alone

whole_construction: All waters [mix/be mixed] with waters; ensuing upper-water relative and male-is predication vs conjoined singular lower water and female-is predication. The editorially bracketed relative before with is text-critical awkwardness, not license to replace all waters with two waters or silently transpose clause units. Upper source noun plural, male copula singular; explain rather than silently repair.
